document: S.R.O. 17(E)/1993, Gazette of India Extraordinary Pt II s.4, 06-12-1993 (downloads/independent-reviewer-D/amend/in.gazette.central.e.1993-12-06.16490/16490.pdf)
purpose: r.22 as substituted (item 5) incl. proviso to (1) on r.180, (3)(a)-(d) and 'or' between proviso conditions (a)/(b); r.25 omitted (item 6); r.26(1) words omitted (item 7)
observed_on_image: Item 5 substitutes r.22: (1) hearing by CO in presence of accused, full liberty to cross-examine, call witnesses, make statement; proviso: where charge arises from a court of inquiry in which r.180 complied with for that accused, CO may dispense with sub-rule (1); (2) dismissal duty and proviso re s.120(2); (3) 'within a reasonable time' (a) s.80 per Appendix III, (b) refer to proper superior military authority, (c) adjourn for evidence to be reduced to writing, (d) if accused below rank of warrant officer, SCM, proviso conditions (a) '...without any reference to that officer; or' (b) grave reason; (4) fresh charges on evidence. Item 6: r.25 omitted. Item 7(i): words 'or (in the case of an officer where there is no summary of evidence) an abstract of the evidence to be adduced' omitted from r.26(1).

document: S.R.O. 17(E)/1993, Gazette of India Extraordinary Pt II s.4, 06-12-1993 (downloads/independent-reviewer-D/amend/in.gazette.central.e.1993-12-06.16490/16490.pdf)
page: PDF p.18, right column lower part
purpose: Exact wording of substituted r.182 as printed (second reading at 300 dpi)
observed_on_image: As printed: '...or answer to a question made or given at a court of inquiry, shall not be admissible in nor shall any evidence respecting the proceedings of the court be given against any such person except upon the trial of such person for wilfully giving false evidence before the court;' The words 'evidence against a person subject to the Act,' (present in the 1954 r.182, MML 2 p.222 and the India Code compilation p.197) do not appear on the Gazette image. Corrigendum not searched.

document: Army Rules 1954 as notified, Gazette of India Pt II s.4, 27-11-1954 (downloads/discovery/ia_in.gazette.central.w.1954-11-27.103686.pdf; archival facsimile of official Gazette)
observed_on_image: r.23(1) evidence of witnesses present before CO 'whether against or for the accused' and other relevant persons taken down in writing in presence and hearing of accused before CO or such officer as he directs; (2) cross-examination; (3) read over, signed; caution wording (reserved CONFLICTING item, not re-read here); (4) English, interpreted; (5) if a person cannot be compelled to attend or attendance cannot in the opinion of the officer taking the summary (to be certified by him in writing) be readily procured, a written statement purporting to be signed by him may be read to the accused and included in the summary; (6) summons. r.24(1)(a)-(c) remand / refer / re-hear; (2) assemble SCM or apply to convene without unnecessary delay.

document: Army Rules 1954 as notified, Gazette of India Pt II s.4, 27-11-1954 (downloads/discovery/ia_in.gazette.central.w.1954-11-27.103686.pdf; archival facsimile of official Gazette)
purpose: r.25 (later omitted), r.26 summary disposal of officers/JCOs/WOs, r.27 delay reports as notified 1954
observed_on_image: r.26(1): where officer/JCO/WO remanded for disposal by authority empowered under s.83, 84 or 85, summary of evidence (or abstract) delivered free with copy of charge as soon as practicable and in any case not less than twenty-four hours before the disposal; (2) authority shall, unless he dismisses the charge or accused consented in writing to dispense with attendance of witnesses, hear the evidence in presence of accused; full liberty to cross-examine, call witnesses, make statement; (3) record per Appendix IV, forward with conduct sheet etc. to superior military authority (s.88). r.27 eight-day delay reports; copy to DJAG from 48th day.

document: Army Rules 1954 as notified, Gazette of India Pt II s.4, 27-11-1954 (downloads/discovery/ia_in.gazette.central.w.1954-11-27.103686.pdf; archival facsimile of official Gazette)
observed_on_image: r.180 full opportunity to be present throughout, make statement, give evidence, cross-examine witnesses affecting character or military reputation, produce witnesses; presiding officer to ensure notice. r.182 (1954) bars CoI proceedings/confession/statement/answer as evidence against a person subject to the Act except on trial for wilfully giving false evidence; NO proviso in the 1954 text.
